The normalized Bernstein coefficients strictly rise before pivotal index M-1, may drop once, then are nondecreasing; subtracting any constant yields at most 3 sign changes. Substitution z=t/(1+t) converts roots in (0,1) into positive roots of a polynomial with those binomial-weighted coefficient signs, so Descartes bounds roots with multiplicity. Bernstein derivative has initially positive sign and at most 2 zeros; hence at most one negative-slope band and at most one two-sided attracting edge equilibrium.
